puzzles.title: The Bog Stone
puzzles.prompt:
Letters are cut into the leaning stone, filled with green moss:

'I have no mouth, yet I swallow the bold.
I have no hands, yet I hold what I hold.
Stand on me lightly, I bear you a while;
Stand on me long and I'll keep you a mile.
What am I?'
puzzles.question: What does the Bog Stone want to hear?
puzzles.customAnswerLabel: Or say your own answer to the stone:
puzzles.knownAnswerLabel: Answer as Grandmother Rook told you: "The bog itself."
puzzles.deductionHint: Think about where you are standing.
puzzles.deductionFailText: You turn the words over and over, but the answer won't come. The stone seems smug about it.
puzzles.wrongAnswerText: Nothing happens, except that the bog burps. You think it is laughing at you.

transcript.speaker: The Bog Stone
transcript.text: The moss in the letters glows green. With a long sucking sound, an old causeway of black stones rises out of the bog, leading west toward a drowned chapel spire.

addJournalChronicle.title: The Stone's Riddle
addJournalChronicle.text: Answered the Bog Stone. A causeway now leads to the Sunken Chapel.
